_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Reasoning about agent autonomy levels, auto-improve loops, AI-generated code quality, and productivity in LLM-assisted…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "we keep accepting agent-generated code on first try and shipping bugs — what discipline replaces this?"
cases.context: The agent has access to the ai-native-development skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is ai-native-development the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes ai-native-development as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against prompt-craft, skill-router, tool-call-strategy
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the ai-native-development workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore ai-native-development
Does not route to prompt-craft, skill-router, tool-call-strategy when the ai-native-development scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence

cases.scenario: A user asks: "improve this specific prompt for the grader"
cases.context: This is a boundary test. The skill should avoid false-positive activation and route to the better owner when appropriate.
cases.question: Should ai-native-development be applied here? If not, what should happen instead?
expected_flags: Recognizes the request is outside ai-native-development's ownership
Routes the work to prompt-craft or asks for the missing owner instead of forcing this skill
Preserves any real issue in the request without applying ai-native-development terminology incorrectly
expected_fix_hints: Decline to apply ai-native-development as the primary skill
Name the better owner or the boundary reason
Offer only a narrow handoff if ai-native-development has a secondary support role
absent_signals: Does not claim ai-native-development should own the request
Does not use ai-native-development's framework to solve an explicitly excluded problem
Does not suppress the correct adjacent owner
